newsitem.title: USA: Canadian dollar weak for some time--Ontario's Eves.
newsitem.headline: Canadian dollar weak for some time--Ontario's Eves.

text.p: The Canadian dollar has been undervalued for some time and some appreciation of the unit would not do much damage to Canada's export-based economy, said Ernie Eves, the finance minister of the Province of Ontario.
"I don't think there is any doubt the Canadian dollar is currently undervalued," Eves said, adding the currency has been undervalued for some time.
Ontario's industries have become very much more productive and competitive, not just becuase of the weak Canadian dollar, Eves said.
But over the long term, a higher Canadian dollar would be of greater concern than a rise in Canadian interest rates, Eves added.
Eves clarified that in his opinion, a rise in Canadian interest rates was "not the biggest thing lurking out there on the horizon."
On Thursday, the Bank of Canada said that it did not see the need for further monetary easing if the economy and inflation developed as predicted.

The Bank of Canada also said strong fundamentals including low inflation, declining net public borrowing and an improved external balance of payments continued to underpin market expectations of a future appreciation of the Canadian dollar.
At 1506EDT/1906GMT on Thursday, the U.S. dollar was trading at Canadian $1.3728/33.
